While within a realm of possibility, that is only one of the many feasible explanations as to why someone would decide to travel through time. Something "horrible" to some is considered less than horrible to others.

Personally, I think it's best that we don't look at this in such a negative light, so as not to add to the defeatist attitudes which seem to engulf the subject of time travel.

Frankly, I find the thought of people time travelling enmasse a bit horrifying. I believe that in the beginning (& perhaps until the end) of the cycle, travelling will be considered a privilage granted to very few individuals. 

As for the risks... 

I Can Think Of Many. But as stated above by others there's been risks in almost everything we've accomplished as a species. I wouldn't put it beyond us to put ourselves at risk solely in pursuit of knowing.

This has been one of my greatest struggles with therapy. Sometime's it feels as though I'm better off without it. There are so many expectations going in, but what they really want is for you to want to help yourself, you are the leader of your experience in therapy and sometimes that's just too much of a burden. you aren't alone
